name: 360 Orbit Staging Guard
author: Jörg Liwa

sections.description:
A copy of a live website contains real customers, real orders and real service credentials. One cron run can send reminder emails to customers, renew subscriptions or call a payment service, silently and without warning. Staging Guard stops that on the copy.

  • Outgoing calls are blocked. Every call that goes through the WordPress HTTP API is refused immediately, except your own address, hosts on your allow list and, by default, WordPress.org (so updates and plugin installation keep working). The log shows which hosts were called and lets you allow one with a click.
  • Emails are caught, not sent. By default nothing leaves the site: each email lands in the Mail catcher tab with its recipients, headers and a safe preview. Alternatively redirect everything to one address, discard it, or let it through.
  • Scheduled tasks are paused. Due WP-Cron events are kept and run once you switch the protection off.
  • Search engines stay away. noindex, an X-Robots-Tag header and a robots.txt that disallows everything. Your Discourage search engines setting is never changed.
  • Visitors can be locked out (optional). Switch it on and everybody except administrators sees a short notice (HTTP 403, noindex) instead of the copy. Let in single IP addresses or ranges (IPv4 and IPv6), or share a secret access link that sets a 7-day cookie, for example for a client who reviews the copy. The page cache is kept out, REST requests and feeds are locked as well. It is off by default.
  • You always know where you are. A red marker in the admin bar shows on every page that the protection is on, and the Status tab says why.
  • A different address only shows a notice. If a copy still has the live settings but runs under another address, the plugin tells you and offers to switch the protection on. It never switches it on by itself, so a domain move of your live site can never silently block its emails.
  • Emergency switch. define( 'WP360_SG_DISABLE', true ); in wp-config.php switches everything off at once.
  • WP-CLI: wp 360-staging status|on|off|auto|hosts|allow <host>|mails.

What this protects, and what it does not

Staging Guard is a safeguard against accidents, not an isolation.

  • It stops what goes through the WordPress HTTP API and wp_mail(). Code that calls curl, file_get_contents() or its own library directly (many payment and cloud SDKs) is not caught.
  • Plugins that talk to a mail service or SMTP directly, or replace wp_mail(), bypass the email protection.
  • The visitor lock covers pages, feeds, sitemaps and the REST API. The login page, the dashboard, scheduled tasks and AJAX requests stay reachable, so nobody gets locked out. Behind a proxy or CDN the IP list sees the proxy, use the access link there.
  • For real isolation, block outgoing traffic in the firewall or remove the service credentials from the copy.

Privacy

Caught emails can contain real customer data. They are stored in your database only, are visible only to administrators (on a multisite network only to super admins), are limited in number and age (50 emails, 7 days by default), never include attachments (only their names) and are removed when you delete the plugin. The log stores host names and counters only, never paths, parameters or content. The plugin itself makes no requests to other servers.

Free vs. Pro

The free version covers everything above.

Staging Guard Pro adds:

  • Service presets for common payment, newsletter, CRM, shipping, backup and AI services, each set to allow or block.
  • Single scheduled tasks can keep running while the rest stays paused.
  • Rules per path and method for allowed hosts (for example only GET on /v1/read).
  • Longer log and mail catcher (up to 500 entries), search, CSV export of the log, .eml export of an email and send as a test to one address.
  • Export and import of the settings for agencies that set up several websites the same way.
  • Automatic update notifications directly in the WordPress admin area.
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin under Plugins → Add New (search for “360 Orbit Staging Guard”), or upload the ZIP under Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin on the staging or development copy. The live address is remembered when you activate it.
  3. Open Staging Guard in the 360 WP Orbit menu and check the status.
  4. Tip: set WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE to staging in the wp-config.php of the copy (define( 'WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE', 'staging' );). WordPress assumes production when nothing is set.
sections.faq:
When is the protection on?

In Automatic mode (the default) the protection is on as long as the environment type is not production. You can also set it to Always on or Off. If the environment type says production but the address differs from the live address, a notice offers to switch the protection on.

The notice says “This site runs under a different address”. What now?

Either click Switch protection on now if this is a copy, or This is the live site if the live site moved to a new address. The second remembers the new address as the live address.

I switched the protection on by mistake on my live site.

Click This is the live site on the Status tab, set the mode to Off, or add define( 'WP360_SG_DISABLE', true ); to wp-config.php.

Where do I see the emails that were caught?

On the Mail catcher tab of the Staging Guard page. HTML emails are shown in a sandboxed preview that loads nothing from the internet and runs no scripts.

Why is WordPress.org allowed?

So that updates and installing plugins keep working on the copy. Blocked calls to WordPress.org also cause warnings when WP_DEBUG is on. You can switch it off in the settings.

An outgoing call still gets through.

Only calls that use the WordPress HTTP API are caught, and redirects are checked as well. Libraries that open connections themselves are not caught. Block them in the firewall, or remove the credentials of that service from the copy.

Does it work on multisite?

The plugin works per site. Activate it on each site where you want to use it. Caught emails can contain password reset links, so on a multisite network only super admins can see them.

What happens when I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Deactivating switches everything off and keeps your settings and caught emails until you delete them on the Mail catcher tab. Deleting the plugin removes its settings, its log and all caught emails.

Liability?

This plugin is provided without any warranty (“as is”). The developer assumes no liability for damage or loss arising from its use. It reduces the risk of accidents on a copy, it does not isolate it.
